column_lineage.transformation: SUM(CASE WHEN pm.paid_flag = 'Y' THEN pm.amount ELSE 0 END)
SUM(pm.amount) - SUM(CASE WHEN pm.paid_flag = 'Y' THEN pm.amount ELSE 0 END)
CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN pm.paid_flag = 'Y' THEN pm.amount ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(pm.amount), 0) AS NUMERIC(9, 2))

summary: This job aggregates monthly premium metrics from staging to calculate total instalments due, collected amounts, outstanding arrears, and collection rate percentages. It produces the rpt.premium_collections table used by the Credit Control and Arrears Review teams.
risk_notes: String Comparison / Collation: T-SQL comparison pm.paid_flag = 'Y' is case-insensitive by default, whereas PySpark is case-sensitive and will exclude 'y' unless upper() or lower() is explicitly applied.

Date Functions & NULL Grouping: DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(pm.due_date), MONTH(pm.due_date), 1) returns NULL if due_date is NULL. Translating to PySpark date_trunc('month', col('due_date')) correctly preserves NULLs, but COUNT(*) inside groups will count rows with NULL dates.

Type Precision & Division: The T-SQL calculation casts division results to DECIMAL(9,2). PySpark division (/) implicitly promotes integer/decimal operands to DoubleType, which can introduce floating-point rounding discrepancies unless explicitly cast to DecimalType(9, 2) or formatted using round/bround.

Division by Zero / NULLIF: PySpark behavior for division by zero depends on spark.sql.ansi.enabled mode (returning NULL vs raising an error). Explicitly porting NULLIF via when(col('amount_due') == 0, lit(null)) is required to ensure consistent cross-environment behavior.
